sources: CRA T4127 Payroll Deductions Formulas (Jan 2026), recorded in salary/ and b4/ · 2026 · federal 20.5% from $58,523 to $117,045; Manitoba 12.75% to $100,000 then 17.4%

CRA 2026 CPP and CPP2 figures (b4/; Payworks, Wagepoint, Canada Pension Map summaries of the CRA rates, search 2026-10-08) · 2026 · CPP 5.95% each side up to YMPE $74,600 (max $4,230.45 employee); CPP2 4% each side on $74,600–$85,000 (max $416 employee, $832 self-employed); no exemption for CPP2

CRA Schedule 8 (combined employment and self-employment earnings; b9/) · 2026 · contributions already made through employment count toward the annual maxima, so self-employment earnings above them add no CPP/CPP2

Calculation (not a CRA rule): b10/calc.py. $10,000 net self-employment income on top of a $100,000 salary (MB, single, 2026): federal 20.5% × $10,000 = $2,050.00; Manitoba: taxable income $98,873 → $108,873, $1,127 at 12.75% + $8,873 at 17.4% = $1,687.59; CPP $0 (salary already above YAMPE). Total $3,737.59 vs $4,161.15 at a $60,000 salary (b9/): $423.56 less. Dependencies: province, other income, credits; the $10K is net of expenses. Verification note: canada.ca cannot be opened from the build machine; check the CRA CPP2 page before publishing.

$100K Salary + $10K Side Hustle: The CPP Surprise
Same $10K Side Hustle, Bigger Salary, Smaller Tax Bill
yt.description:
Same $10,000 side hustle. Bigger salary. Smaller tax bill. Here's why (Manitoba, 2026).

On top of a $100,000 salary, the extra $10,000 pays federal tax at 20.5% ($2,050) and Manitoba tax at 12.75% / 17.4% ($1,688). But CPP: $0. Your job already paid the maximum CPP and CPP2 for the year, so self-employment income above it adds no contributions.

Total: $3,738. On a $60,000 salary the same $10,000 cost $4,161, including $1,190 of CPP. That's $424 less at the higher salary.

Same $10K in Alberta or Ontario? Pick one in the comments and we'll run it next.

Sources: CRA T4127 (2026 rates), CRA CPP/CPP2 2026, Schedule 8. Example only (Manitoba, single, $10K net); general information, not tax advice.
